text: The split of RWB-E4-045 is read as AC1 owned by RWB-ITG-E4045-ITG and AC2 owned by this application story, and the calculation behind AC1 is built and tested here on a synthetic fee set of this run: case RC-2026-000555 of account A-0555, one court fee fact with a fee row in force at a stated version, producing one decision record and one proceeds row with matched_to FEE. The fee detail behind the generic legacy lines is filled from FSD P8 A2.5 and TSD P8 T3.1, and the four legacy test case IDs keep their own rows in the Test Cases master.
why: Both legacy criteria are generic, the four legacy test cases carry no case, fee type, amount or date, the FSD main success criterion is one line marked 'Written one epic ahead', and the split plan gives this slice AC2 only, so the calculation cannot be built or tested without a stated set.

text: The fee rows are versioned reference data of rwb-case, read on its reference-data contract; the partner facts are read on rwb-partner's contract; both are consumed reads with a one-hop 2 s contract and a breaker, built against their fakes; no fee table is declared in rwb_payment and the service holds no copy of a fee row; the payment and account fee facts are read on the service's own views recovery.v_ace_account and recovery.v_ace_payment.
why: The feature is specified as fee tables held as data, the ownership map gives this service only proceeds, and no source publishes the read operations that carry the fee rows or the partner facts, so the baseline has to state where they come from to be buildable.
read: FSD P8 v3 A2.5.1 and A2.5.2; TSD P8 v2 T3.1 and T5.2; context pack P8 tables and operations; Template and Rules R3 default ruling
confirm: P8 data owner, the P3 reference-data owner and the P8 solution architect at the contract tag review
impact: The consumed rows, the fakes and the absence of a fee table in rwb_payment; the two provided operations, the base and the rights are unchanged

text: A fee row in force carries the fee type, the rate or flat amount, the cap and the validity dates, and its version; the calculation reads that row at run time and records the row identity and its version with the answer; no rate, cap, tolerance or fee type is a constant of the build; the service reads no rule package for this step and holds no copy of the fee rows or of rule_row.
why: No source publishes a fee type list, a fee row value or a threshold, the legacy data table names rule_row while the feature is specified on fee tables held as data, and the action cannot be evaluated, asserted or reviewed without a stated reading.
read: FSD P8 v3 A2.5.3.1 BR-P8-005; TSD P8 v2 T3.2; legacy RWB-E4-045 Data table; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-41 and R-LIT-42
confirm: the reference-data owner, the P7 rule owner and the P8 business analyst at the fee data review
impact: The source of the amount, the content of the record and the absence of a rule package in this step; the criteria, the messages and the 2 s budget are unchanged

text: The calculation publishes nothing and adds no operation: the answer is the local decision record of DP-03 plus the proceeds row with matched_to FEE, and the posting and matching stories of the service read them on their own paths; no topic, no event name and no fee operation is declared by this story, and a fee event, if the programme wants one, is left to the service contract baseline.
why: The service owns three events, none of them a fee event, and two operations, neither of them a fee operation, and the ownership map is the authority, so a carrier cannot be invented for the answer.
read: Context pack P8 operations and events; TSD P8 v2 T5.3 and T-A.1; FSD P8 v3 A2.5.2
confirm: P8 solution architect and the service contract owner at the contract tag review
impact: The carrier of the answer and the call-type summary; the schema, the rights and the criteria are unchanged

text: The calculation is one event-started Temporal workflow per fee fact on queue rwb-payment in namespace rwb-recovery, with one calculation activity that writes the decision record and the proceeds row in one transaction; the fee fact arrives from the route owner's topic, the daily cadence stays with the ACE batch completion read on recovery.v_ace_batch_status (AceDataReady, EV-26), there is no Temporal Schedule and no Quartz row, and the workflow and activity names are set at build and carried as placeholders until then.
why: The context pack lists two jobs and zero workflows, no source names the fee run or its activity, and the FSD and the routing logic state the trigger of the calculation two different ways, so the baseline has to fix one reading to be testable.
